Event Description: On 9 November 1989, East German authorities announced that citizens could cross the heavily fortified Berlin Wall, prompting thousands of East Berliners to surge toward the checkpoints. Over the next hours, border guards, overwhelmed by the crowds, opened the gates, allowing people from both sides to reunite, climb the concrete barrier, and dismantle sections with hammers and chisels. The peaceful breach symbolized the collapse of the communist regime in the German Democratic Republic and accelerated the reunification process, which was formally completed on 3 October 1990. The event marked a decisive moment in the end of the Cold War, influencing democratic movements across Eastern Europe and reshaping the geopolitical landscape of the continent.
